diagnosis_explanation: Your liver problem is very serious. It means your liver was not working well. This caused other problems. Your body had too much swelling. Your body also had low blood pressure. Your body did not have enough protein. Your body did not have enough red blood cells. You also had trouble breathing. These problems are getting better.
medication_rationale:
Protonix 40 mg:
This medicine helps your stomach make less acid.
It can help your stomach feel better.
You may get a headache or diarrhea.
This is normal.

Metoclopramide 10 mg:
This medicine helps your stomach empty faster.
It can help with nausea or vomiting.
You might feel sleepy or tired.
Call your doctor if you have jerky movements.
Also call if you get a rash.

Zyvox 600 mg:
This medicine fights a type of infection.
It is an antibiotic.
You will take this medicine for 5 days.
Call your doctor if you get a rash.
Also call if you have stomach pain.

Diflucan 150 mg:
This medicine fights fungal infections.
It is an antifungal medicine.
You will take this medicine for 3 days.
You may get a headache or an upset stomach.
Call your doctor if you get a rash.

Bumex 2 mg:
This medicine helps your body get rid of extra fluid.
It can help with swelling.
You may urinate more often. This is normal.
Call your doctor if you feel dizzy.
Also call if you get leg cramps.

Megace 400 mg:
This medicine can help with appetite.
It may help you gain weight.
You might have diarrhea or feel sick.
Call your doctor if you get a rash.

Ensure 1:
This is a nutritional drink.
It provides extra calories and nutrients.
Drink it with your meals.

MiraLax 17 gm:
This medicine helps you have bowel movements.
It is a laxative.
You might get gas or bloating.
Call your doctor if you have stomach pain.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel very tired this week.
- You may have some discomfort as your body heals.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 5 pounds.
- Walk for 5 minutes inside your home 2 times a day.
- Your doctor is lowering your IV fluids.
- You may have some swelling in your legs and feet.
- Call your doctor if you feel much worse or have trouble breathing.

**Week 2:**
- You may start to feel a little more energy.
- Swelling in your legs and feet should start to go down.
- Continue to walk 5 minutes inside your home 2 times a day.
- Keep lifting no more than 5 pounds.
- Drink fluids as your doctor directs.
- Your goal is to walk a bit longer each day.
- Call your doctor if swelling gets worse or breathing is hard.

**Week 3:**
- You should have more energy than last week.
- Your discomfort should be less noticeable.
- You can walk for 10 minutes inside your home 2 times a day.
- Keep lifting no more than 5 pounds.
- Eat foods low in salt to help with swelling.
- Your goal is to walk around your home without needing to rest.
- Call your doctor if you have sudden trouble breathing or new chest pain.

**Week 4:**
- You may feel much stronger and more comfortable.
- You can likely do light tasks around the house.
- You can walk for 15 minutes inside your home 2 times a day.
- Continue to avoid lifting more than 5 pounds.
- Keep your salt intake low.
- Your goal is to walk outside for short periods.
- Call your doctor if swelling returns or breathing becomes difficult.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Most people start to feel much better in 4 to 6 weeks.
- Keep following your doctor's plan for fluids and salt.
- Slowly increase your walking and activity each week.
- Rest when you need to.
